---
title: "Installation"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

quartifyr is a single installable R package bundling a Quarto extension
and a Python engine; install only the pieces you need.

## 1. Quarto extension only

If you just want the shell-generation pieces (title page, signature
pages, synopsis, numbered appendices, header/footer), this is a regular
Quarto extension:

```bash
quarto add jprybylski/quartifyr
```

Or, once the R package itself is installed (step 3 below):

```r
quartifyr::install_quartifyr_extension()
```

It composes with [A2-ai's `quarto-plus`](https://github.com/A2-ai/quarto-plus)
for ToC/list of figures/list of tables/abbreviations rather than
duplicating them, so install that too:

```bash
quarto add A2-ai/quarto-plus
```

With nothing else installed you can already render a real, styled shell;
see the repo README's Quick Start. The only other prerequisite is
[Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) itself.

## 2. `inst/python/`: the reference-doc builder (standalone)

The Python engine behind `styling_build_reference_docx()`/etc. is also
independently pip/uv-installable, if you'd rather not go through R:

```bash
# from a checkout of the repo
uv venv .venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e '.[dev]'
```

This gets you the `quartifyr-styling` CLI; see [Styling](styling.html)
for its subcommands.

## 3. The `quartifyr` R package

```r
pak::pkg_install("local::/path/to/quartifyr")   # or remotes::install_local()
```

Pulls in [`reportifyr`](https://github.com/A2-ai/reportifyr) and
[`pyro`](https://github.com/A2-ai/pyro) transitively (neither has a CRAN
release; both resolve from `a2-ai.r-universe.dev`, declared in
`DESCRIPTION`'s `Additional_repositories:`). This is a convenience
wrapper around Quarto + the Python engine + `reportifyr`; see [The R
package](r-package.html). It's optional; you can call the underlying
pieces yourself instead.

The `quartifyr` R package itself is **not** `renv`-managed -- install it
into each report project's own `renv` library explicitly, from that
project's directory:

```r
renv::install("local::/path/to/quartifyr")
```

## Full toolchain, end to end

For the complete two-pass pipeline (real tables/figures/footnotes
filled in, not just the shell):

```bash
# 1. Install the quartifyr R package itself
Rscript -e 'pak::pkg_install("local::.")'   # from this checkout's root

# 2. Run the demo end to end
cd examples/demo-report
Rscript -e 'renv::restore()'
Rscript -e 'renv::install("local::../..")'
Rscript -e 'reportifyr::initialize_report_project(project_dir = getwd())'   # first clone only
Rscript -e 'quartifyr::initialize_quartifyr_project(getwd())'              # first clone only
Rscript render.R --final
# -> report/draft/report-draft.docx, report/final/report-final.docx
```

Or just run the demo's own smoke test, which does step 2 for you and
asserts the output is actually correct:

```bash
python3 examples/demo-report/smoke_test.py
```

See [Examples](examples.html) for what this produces.
